Order No. 06 Dated: 16.08.2023

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to release the amount of compensation in favour of the petitioner in lieu of acquisition of his land measuring an area of 0.016 acre being part of R.S. Plot No. 1597 under R.S. Khata No. 260, Mouza-Raghunathpur, P.S.-Nimdih, District- Seraikella-Kharsawan (hereinafter referred to as "the said land").
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that on 30.07.2005, a permission was sought from the competent authority under Section 46 of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 for sale of the said land in favour of the petitioner.
Subsequently, Smt. Kalo Mahlani sold 3 decimals of the said land to the petitioner on 29.10.2005 by way of registered sale deed.
Thereafter, the petitioner got his name mutated on 19.06.2009 and started paying rent to the government.
The petitioner has been issued rent receipts with respect to the said land from 2010-11 to 2015-16.

3. It is also submitted that a notification under Section 3-D(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act, 1956") was issued on 15.02.2016 for acquisition of land of Mouza- Raghunathpur (Annexure-4 to the writ petition).

Seraikella-Kharsawan-cum-competent authority with regard to preparation of award and to receive compensation. The petitioner represented the concerned authorities including the respondent nos. 2 and 3, however, the said representations remained unresponded, which has compelled him to prefer the present writ petition.

4. It is jointly submitted by learned counsel for the respondent nos. 1 to 3 as well as the respondent no. 4 that the factual contention raised by the petitioner in the present writ petition is required to be verified by the respondent no. 3.
Hence, if the petitioner prefers a fresh representation in this regard before the respondent no. 3, an appropriate order in accordance with law will be passed within a timeframe.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the case, the petitioner is given liberty to prefer a fresh representation on the present issue before the respondent no. 3.

On receipt of the said representation, the respondent no. 3, after providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner/his representative and on verifying the relevant record, shall take appropriate informed decision within eight weeks from the date of filing of the said representation.
6. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of with aforesaid liberty and direction.
